final_answer:
Let
\[
P_t(z)=0
\]
for some \(z\in S^{2m-1}\). Write \(r_j=|z_j|\). From
\[
z_j^2=-t\overline{z_{j+1}}
\]
we get
\[
r_j^2=t r_{j+1}.
\]
No \(r_j\) can be \(0\), since then all would be \(0\). Taking logs gives
\[
\log r_{j+1}=2\log r_j-\log t.
\]
Iterating cyclically forces \(\log r_j=\log t\) for every \(j\), hence \(r_j=t\). Since \(z\in S^{2m-1}\),
\[
m t^2=1.
\]
Thus zeros on the sphere can occur only when
\[
t=\frac1{\sqrt m}.
\]
They do occur then: if \(z_j=t e^{i\theta_j}\), the phase condition is
\[
\theta_{j+1}\equiv -2\theta_j-\pi \pmod{2\pi},
\]
and this cyclic recurrence has solutions. Therefore the assumption \(P_t\neq0\) means exactly
\[
t\ne \frac1{\sqrt m}.
\]

So the degree is constant on the two intervals
\[
0<t<\frac1{\sqrt m},\qquad t>\frac1{\sqrt m}.
\]

For \(0<t<1/\sqrt m\), homotope to \(t=0\):
\[
P_0(z)=(z_1^2,\dots,z_m^2).
\]
The normalized map has degree \(2^m\): a regular value with all coordinates nonzero has exactly \(2^m\) preimages, and the map is holomorphic in each coordinate, so each local degree is \(+1\).

For \(t>1/\sqrt m\), divide by \(t\) and homotope to
\[
(z_1,\dots,z_m)\mapsto (\overline{z_2},\overline{z_3},\dots,\overline{z_1}).
\]
The cyclic coordinate permutation has real determinant \(+1\), while complex conjugation in each of the \(m\) coordinates has real determinant \(-1\). Hence the degree is
\[
(-1)^m.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\deg(F_t)=
\begin{cases}
2^m, & 0<t<\dfrac1{\sqrt m},\\[4pt]
(-1)^m, & t>\dfrac1{\sqrt m}.
\end{cases}
}
\]
At \(t=1/\sqrt m\), the assumption fails, so \(F_t\) is not defined on all of \(S^{2m-1}\).
